slides.kicker: Twelve tabs open. None of them the one.
slides.title:
Why can't I just
[[focus]] on
the thing?
slides.sub: You are not unfocused. You are focused on everything.

slides.title:
Attention is not
a [[dial]] you
turn up
slides.body: You have heard "concentrate harder" since primary school. If effort alone worked, it would have by now. Attention in ADHD is not low. It is unregulated.

slides.title:
You do not lack
focus. You lack
a [[filter]]
slides.body: The fridge hum, the notification, the thought about lunch: they all arrive at the same volume as the task. Nothing is muted, so everything competes.

slides.title:
Interesting beats
[[important]],
every time
slides.body: Your brain runs on interest, novelty and urgency, not on priority. That is why you can lose three hours to a rabbit hole and three minutes to a report.

slides.title:
The distraction
is usually a
[[relief]]
slides.body: A task that is boring or unclear is uncomfortable to hold. Your attention leaves it the way a hand leaves a hot pan. It is escape, not failure.

slides.title:
Make the task
[[louder]] than
the room
slides.body: One window. One tab. Phone in another room, not face down. You cannot out-will a distraction, but you can make it walk further to reach you.

slides.title:
Give your focus
an [[edge]] to
lean on
slides.body: A timer running. A person working beside you. A deadline that is real today, not next month. External pressure is what your brain was waiting for.

slides.title:
Catch the drift
[[early]], not
an hour later
slides.body: You will drift. The skill is noticing sooner. A note on the desk saying what you were doing turns an hour lost into a minute lost.

slides.title:
Save this for the
next time you
[[wander off]]
slides.body: Your attention is not broken. It just needs a smaller room. Dump everything into my.adhd and get one thing back to point it at.
